hints: Notice what is given at end R: charge $Q$ in time $t$, and that the wire carries a constant electric current despite area $A$ changing to $A/2$.
Connect this to $I = Q/t$: constant current means the same charge per unit time must pass any cross-section of the series wire.
Find $I$ from the R data as $Q/t$, then multiply that same $I$ by the new time $t/4$ to get the charge at S.
walkthrough: Identify the current from end R using $I = Q/t$. Charge $Q$ passes in time $t$, so the rate of flow is $Q/t$.
Apply charge conservation for a constant current: the same current exists at end S as at end R. The smaller area $A/2$ makes drift speed larger but does not change $I$.
Set up charge at S as $Q_S = I \times \Delta t$ with $\Delta t = t/4$.

A.explanation: Divides by 8 by combining the factor 1/4 from time with an extra factor 1/2 from area, but area does not change the current.

B.explanation: Current is the same at R and S, so $I = Q/t$ gives charge $I \times t/4 = Q/4$ at S.

C.explanation: Uses only the area ratio $A/2$, but charge flow rate is unchanged and the time interval is $t/4$.

D.explanation: Assumes the same charge $Q$ passes in any time, ignoring that the time interval at S is only $t/4$.
